editorial.description_en: Rock stained by iron running over it for years. Dark, red, and mineral rather than organic.
editorial.description_ja: 鉄で赤くなった岩のような、暗い赤茶。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.456, C 0.088, h 38.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 錆 (sabi, rust) + 岩 (iwa, rock). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Rusted Rock" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 錆岩. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — yama-moe at ΔE00 6.7, koi-tsuchi at ΔE00 7.7, furu-kawa at ΔE00 8.2. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (218°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
